summary: The 900 s run shows the intended sequence working through fill, wait, transfer, stop/resume, drain, inter-cycle restart, second stop, and SHUT, and it ends in IDLE with all valves closed. The first fill reached 0.80 m and transfer began after the 10 s wait at 180.000000038 s, the STOP from about 220.1 s to 280.1 s held all three valves closed, the restart at 280.1 s resumed transfer, the first drain ended at 630.000000214 s and filling restarted at 638.000000216 s after an 8 s delay, and SHUT at 700.000000000 s commanded V2 and V3 open with V1 closed until both tanks were at or below low level, then returned to IDLE at about 716.0 s. The run is only partially valid because one resolved acceptance check was not met exactly: the STOP was specified for 220 s and the resume START for 280 s, but the actual controller transitions and valve closures/openings occurred at about 220.1 s and 280.1 s instead of exactly those times.
issues: AC-03 was not satisfied exactly at t=280.0 s as specified. The interrupted transfer resumed at t=280.0999999999952 s, when controller_state changed back to 4 and valve2_open returned to 100; there is no event at exactly 280.0 s for the actual transfer resumption.

The exact stop-time requirement stated in the brief was not met at 220 s. The STOP command input changed at t=220.0000000221015 s, but the controller did not enter PAUSED and close V2 until t=220.0999999999918 s; valve2_open stayed at 100 until that later time.

Because the first STOP took effect at about 220.1 s rather than 220.0 s, AC-02 as written for the STOP interval 'after 220 s' is not exact at the interval boundary: from 220.000000022 s to 220.099999999 s, V2 remained open at 100.

If AC-06 is interpreted at exactly t=700.0 s with zero tolerance, the actual command change occurs at t=700.0000000000906 s rather than exactly 700.0 s. At that event V1 stayed 0 and V2/V3 became 100, but the trace does not show the change at exactly 700.0000000000000 s.
assumptions: The executable model used 0.80 m as the Tank 1 high setpoint for the TP17 demonstration configuration, retaining 0.78 m only as older conflicting evidence outside this run configuration.
The executable model used 8 s as the inter-cycle wait after Tank 2 low for the TP17 demonstration configuration, retaining 10 s only as conflicting evidence outside this run configuration.
The executable model used 10 s as the wait after Tank 1 low / post-transfer wait for this configuration, per clarify-stage decision.

The model used the legacy-demo continuous relationships and nominal parameters A1=1.20 m2, A2=1.40 m2, qFill=0.0060 m3/s, qTransfer=0.0045 m3/s, and qDrain=0.0050 m3/s because no other governing plant physics were directly stated.
The plant was modeled in signal-flow level form rather than an acausal hydraulic network, based on the explicit legacy differential equations and absence of pressure-loss/hydraulic parameters.

The model implemented sampled PLC command handling with latched sampled Boolean variables and one-scan pulses; the observed ~0.1 s offsets in response are consistent with that sampled execution choice.

controller_state was represented as Integer codes 1..9 instead of a string report variable, with the stated mapping 1 IDLE, 2 FILL_T1, 3 WAIT_AFTER_FILL, 4 TRANSFER_T1_T2, 5 WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER, 6 DRAIN_T2, 7 WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN, 8 PAUSED, 9 SHUTDOWN.

Derived from the trajectory: SHUT draining from 700.0000000000906 s to 715.9999997120988 s implies the model assumed the shutdown-completion criterion was simply both tanks at or below the 0.05 m low thresholds under the fixed nominal transfer/drain rates, with no extra hold time before returning to IDLE.
root_causes: The timing misses come from the model's sampled PLC implementation rather than the sequence logic itself. The command tables apply button changes at 220.000000022 s and 280.000000028 s, but the controller acts on sampled pulses at 220.0999999999918 s and 280.0999999999952 s, showing about one 0.1 s scan delay before mode changes and valve commands update.

The first STOP interval is not exact at the 220 s boundary because transfer remained active until the sampled STOP pulse was processed. That is why der(tank1.level) stayed at -0.00375 m/s, der(tank2.level) stayed at +0.003214 m/s, and valve2_open stayed at 100 until 220.0999999999918 s.

The resume event is similarly delayed because START at 280.000000028 s was not acted on until the next sample/pulse evaluation at 280.0999999999952 s. At that point controller_state returned to 4 (TRANSFER_T1_T2) and valve2 reopened, so the control context was preserved correctly but not at the exact requested timestamp.

The SHUT command behavior itself is correct in logic, but any zero-tolerance reading of AC-06 fails for the same numerical/sampling reason: the event is recorded at 700.0000000000906 s, not exactly 700.0 s. Once sampled, the model correctly inhibited V1 and opened V2 and V3 together, giving der(tank1.level) = -0.00375 m/s and der(tank2.level) = -0.000357 m/s until both tanks reached low level.
